sections.content: When most real estate investors think about hot markets, they picture Phoenix, Tampa, or Nashville. Great Falls, Montana rarely makes that list — and that is exactly what makes it interesting. This mid-sized city of roughly 60,000 people sits along the Missouri River in north-central Montana, and it offers something increasingly rare in today's market: affordable entry prices, steady rental demand, and room to grow. Whether you are brand new to the game and just working through a [Real Estate Investing for Beginners](https://aiwholesail.com/guides/real-estate-investing-for-beginners) guide, or you are a seasoned wholesaler looking for your next market, Great Falls deserves a serious look.
Great Falls MT Market Overview: What Investors Need to Know

Great Falls is the third-largest city in Montana and serves as the commercial and healthcare hub for a wide rural region. Malmstrom Air Force Base is one of the city's biggest economic anchors, employing thousands of military personnel and civilian workers. That military presence creates a consistent, reliable pool of renters — people who typically pay on time, take care of properties, and rotate through every two to three years, keeping vacancy rates low and demand steady. The local economy is also supported by healthcare, agriculture, retail, and a growing small business sector.

The housing market in Great Falls has seen moderate appreciation over the past few years, following national trends but without the extreme volatility seen in larger metros. Inventory has tightened compared to pre-pandemic levels, but the market remains far more accessible than Bozeman or Missoula, where prices have surged dramatically. For investors, that affordability gap is a major opportunity. You can still find deals here that make financial sense without needing to stretch your numbers.
Average Home Prices in Great Falls MT

As of 2024, the median home price in Great Falls sits around $265,000 to $290,000 — well below the Montana statewide median, which has been pushed higher by resort towns and Bozeman's tech boom. Distressed properties and fixer-uppers can still be found in the $120,000 to $180,000 range, making them attractive targets for wholesalers and flippers. Rental rates for a single-family home typically run between $1,100 and $1,700 per month depending on size, condition, and neighborhood, giving investors a realistic path to positive cash flow when they buy right.

Best Neighborhoods for Real Estate Investors in Great Falls
Not every zip code in Great Falls performs the same way. Here is a breakdown of the key areas investors should focus on, depending on their strategy.
Southside: Value Plays and Rental Demand

The Southside neighborhoods offer some of the most affordable housing stock in the city. You will find older homes — many built in the 1940s through 1970s — with lower purchase prices and strong rental demand from working-class residents and military families. Renovation costs can add up with older properties, so due diligence on mechanicals, roofing, and foundation is critical. But when you find the right deal, buy-and-hold investors can generate solid cash-on-cash returns here.
Westside: Stable Rentals Near Malmstrom

The Westside sits close to Malmstrom Air Force Base, making it a prime rental market. Military tenants often prefer this area for its proximity to the base, and BAH (Basic Allowance for Housing) rates help support rents. Homes here tend to be post-war bungalows and ranch-style houses in the $180,000 to $250,000 range. For buy-and-hold investors, this is one of the more predictable neighborhoods in the city.
Riverview and North Side: Flip Opportunities

The Riverview area and parts of the North Side have seen increased buyer interest from owner-occupants and move-up buyers. These neighborhoods offer more attractive streetscapes, larger lots, and proximity to parks and the river trail system. Light cosmetic flips — updated kitchens, bathrooms, paint, and flooring — can generate solid spreads when properties are purchased below market. ARVs in renovated homes in these areas can push into the $300,000 to $380,000 range depending on size and finishes.
Types of Real Estate Deals Available in Great Falls MT

items: Wholesale Deals: Motivated sellers do exist in Great Falls — estate sales, tax-delinquent properties, tired landlords, and pre-foreclosures create opportunities for wholesalers to put properties under contract and assign them to cash buyers. Check out our guide on [Wholesaling Real Estate for Beginners](https://aiwholesail.com/guides/wholesaling-real-estate-for-beginners) to understand the mechanics before diving in.

Fix and Flip: Older housing stock throughout the city means there is no shortage of properties needing cosmetic or moderate renovation. Flippers who can manage contractors remotely — or who have a trusted local team — can find deals that deliver $30,000 to $60,000 in profit after holding costs.

Buy and Hold Rentals: With Malmstrom AFB driving consistent rental demand and median rents rising gradually, buy-and-hold is arguably the strongest long-term strategy in this market. DSCR loans make financing easier for out-of-state investors.

Small Multifamily: Duplexes and small apartment buildings occasionally come to market and can be compelling for investors looking to scale their rental portfolio. Values are still reasonable compared to larger Montana cities.

Off-Market Deals: Many of the best opportunities never hit the MLS. Learning [how to find off-market real estate deals](https://aiwholesail.com/guides/off-market-real-estate-deals) through direct mail, driving for dollars, and local networking can give you a serious edge in this market.

sections.content: Local Market Trends in Great Falls MT

Great Falls has not experienced the dramatic price spikes seen in Bozeman or Missoula, but the market has shifted noticeably since 2020. Median prices climbed roughly 25 to 35 percent from 2020 to 2023 before leveling off as interest rates rose. Days on market have increased compared to the frenzied 2021 and 2022 period, giving buyers more time and leverage in negotiations — which is good news for investors hunting deals. Rental vacancy rates remain low, hovering around 3 to 5 percent, which supports rent levels and makes the buy-and-hold case attractive.

One trend worth watching: remote workers and lifestyle buyers from Seattle, Denver, and other expensive metros have been moving to smaller Montana cities in search of affordability and quality of life. While Great Falls has attracted fewer of these transplants than Bozeman, the trend is real and could support further price appreciation over the next five to ten years. Investors who get in now are positioning ahead of that curve.

"The best deals are found in markets that other investors have not discovered yet. By the time everyone agrees a market is great, the best opportunities are already gone." — Common wisdom among experienced real estate investors
Practical Tips for Out-of-State Investors Targeting Great Falls
Investing remotely is more doable than ever, but it requires a disciplined approach. Here are the most important steps for out-of-state investors looking at real estate deals in Great Falls MT.

items: Build a local team first: Find a real estate agent who works with investors (not just retail buyers), a reliable property manager, and a general contractor before you close your first deal. Your team is your eyes and ears on the ground.

Understand the true cost of older homes: Great Falls has a lot of housing stock built before 1980. Budget carefully for potential issues like knob-and-tube wiring, galvanized plumbing, and older HVAC systems. A thorough inspection is non-negotiable.

Analyze every deal conservatively: Use tools like our free [Wholesale Deal Calculator](https://aiwholesail.com/tools/wholesale-deal-calculator) to stress-test your numbers before making offers. Factor in a longer-than-expected rehab timeline and higher contingency reserves for older properties.

Leverage the MLS and off-market channels together: Do not rely solely on listed properties. The best deals in any market — including Great Falls — often come through direct mail campaigns, probate leads, or relationships with local wholesalers.

Visit the market at least once: Even one trip to Great Falls to walk neighborhoods, meet your team, and see properties in person will dramatically sharpen your judgment. What looks great on paper sometimes tells a different story in person.

Research Malmstrom AFB housing allowances: Military BAH rates are published publicly and can help you gauge what military tenants can afford, giving you a reliable ceiling for rents in military-adjacent neighborhoods.

Learn how to analyze deals properly: Read our guide on [how to analyze real estate deals like a pro](https://aiwholesail.com/guides/how-to-analyze-real-estate-deals) to make sure you are not missing hidden costs or leaving money on the table.

Relationships with local investors and agents in Great Falls will surface deals and market intelligence you cannot find anywhere else. Is Great Falls MT the Right Market for You?

Great Falls is not going to make you rich overnight, and it is not the kind of market that grabs headlines at real estate conferences. But that is actually the point. This is a steady, fundamentals-driven market with affordable entry prices, genuine rental demand anchored by a military base, and a housing stock that still produces the kind of distressed deals that make wholesaling and flipping viable. For investors who do their homework, build a solid local team, and run their numbers carefully, real estate deals in Great Falls MT can deliver reliable returns without the competition or price pressure of Montana's more glamorous markets.
